correctness.rationale: For half-sides a≥b and center c, the vertical half-extent |u_y|+|v_y| is ≥b, and the maximum squared vertex norm is at least |c|²+a²+b²+2b|c| by the orthonormal component inequality. Hence a same-area feasible horizontal rectangle can be centered if h+b≤0, and can be placed with bottom h and top h+2b otherwise: the vertex bound then gives a²+(h+2b)²≤1 and h+2b>|h|. This proves the needed unrestricted reduction for every orientation and translation. With t the largest absolute endpoint height, the sharp area envelope is 2 sqrt(1−t²) min(2t,t−h). The interior optima of its two smooth branches are t=1/sqrt(2) and t=q; the second derivative test is not needed to select regimes because the branch derivatives change sign once and the second branch derivative at t=−h has sign 1−3h². This yields the three branches and the two transitions. Equality in the vertex bound plus the cutting constraint forces vertical half-extent b when h>−1/sqrt(2); in the centered comparison case use a²+b²=1, c=0 and b=−h. Thus the short side is vertical and the optimizer unique after the first threshold, including at the second. Before the first, equality of the disk bound gives exactly centered inscribed squares that pass the cut; at the first only the aligned square fits. Differentiation gives the stated one-sided second derivatives (on the last branch M′=−2 sqrt(1−q²), q′=q/(4q−h)); expansion q=1−(1−h)/3+O((1−h)²) and the cap-area integral yield the stated constants. value.rationale: For a classical curved family, the key obstruction is the free orientation, not finding a stationary height under a chosen axis. The same-area comparison resolves that obstruction and yields uniqueness and distinct contact thresholds as well as differentiability and thin-cap utilization for the actual unrestricted optimum. The result is more than an isolated semicircle value or a box-finding algorithm.
